requirements.title: Launch prologue runs six steps in a fixed, load-bearing order before any window exists
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/DroppyCodeApp.swift:3-19 @main struct DroppyCodeApp.init() - the whole prologue, in order: DCInstallNotificationGuard(), signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN), WebsiteCaptures.prepare(), LegacyMigration.run(), HangWatchdog.start(), SwitchLatency.start()
DroppyCode/App/DroppyCodeApp.swift:8-9 comment - 'Before anything posts a notification'
DroppyCode/App/DroppyCodeApp.swift:13 comment - 'Before anything reads settings or the library.'
requirements.preconditions: Process has started; no window, no AppModel and no settings read has happened yet. AppDelegate is attached with @NSApplicationDelegateAdaptor (DroppyCodeApp.swift:5) but applicationDidFinishLaunching has not run.
requirements.action: The process enters the app entry point.
requirements.expected_result: Exactly these six steps run, in this order, synchronously on the main thread, before the scene body is evaluated and before applicationDidFinishLaunching: (1) DCInstallNotificationGuard(), (2) signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN), (3) WebsiteCaptures.prepare(), (4) LegacyMigration.run(), (5) HangWatchdog.start(), (6) SwitchLatency.start(). No other work happens first. The ordering is stated by the source's own comments as load-bearing: the notification guard must precede any posted notification, and the capture prep plus legacy migration must precede any read of settings or the library.
side_effects: Installs a process-wide NSNotificationCenter guard (see PR-LAUNCH-002)
Changes the SIGPIPE disposition process-wide (see PR-LAUNCH-003)
May create capture scratch directories and wipe a defaults suite (see PR-LAUNCH-008)
May copy UserDefaults keys and move an Application Support folder (see PR-LAUNCH-011, PR-LAUNCH-012)
Spawns the hang-watchdog background thread (see PR-LAUNCH-014)
requirements.persistence: Only through the steps it calls; the prologue itself persists nothing.
failure_cases: No step reports failure to the caller; every one of the six is a void call with its own internal try?/guard handling. A failure inside any step cannot abort launch.
requirements.windows_path: A single startup function called before the main window is created and before the settings/library store is first touched, keeping the same relative order for the steps that are ported. Step 1 (an Objective-C exception net) has no Windows analogue and is not ported (port_impacts.md:384 entry 188); step 2 has no Windows analogue (no SIGPIPE) and is replaced by the pipe-write error handling recorded in platform_adaptations PA-0004. Step 3 (WebsiteCaptures.prepare()) is not ported: the capture subsystem is not ported (engineering_decisions.md ED-001, see PR-LAUNCH-008). Step 4 (LegacyMigration.run()) is not ported: BLK-0005 is NOT_APPLICABLE_WITH_EVIDENCE under OD-0008 A5 (see PR-LAUNCH-009 to PR-LAUNCH-013). Step 6 (SwitchLatency.start()) is not ported: it is inert outside the development build (engineering_decisions.md ED-005, see PR-LAUNCH-022). Step 5 (HangWatchdog.start()) is the one step ported as a call in the startup function.
requirements.verification_method: unit test on the startup function asserting that HangWatchdog.start() runs in it and that the function returns before the main window is created; restart test asserting no settings or library read occurs before the startup function returns
